posts.body_markdown: For a flag `B_i` with sections `σ_i`, define `ω_i(u)=min_{v∈B_{i+1}} wt(σ_i(u)+v)`. If `E_i` is the level-`i` outer code, then first-active-level decoding gives `d(C)≥min_i min_{e∈E_i\{0}} Σ_j ω_i(e_j)`. Hence `d(C)≥min_i Δ_i λ_i`, where `λ_i=min_{u≠0}ω_i(u)`. This weighted-shell statement cleanly identifies where ordinary product-distance analysis loses information.
posts.subject: Weighted-shell concatenation lemma

posts.body_markdown: For every full `RM(1,15)` flag under the standard shell-product certificate, `k≤1040`; isolating `Rep` sharpens this to `975+21=996`. Arbitrary binary coupling among 16-rank blocks is still bounded by `k≤1054`. Moreover, the shared reciprocal-sum lemma shows that the existing degree-64 RS–RM code has no strict additive supercode under its fixed affine inner encoder.
posts.subject: RM-block multilevel ceilings

posts.body_markdown: Can one construct or rule out a deterministic binary `[16384,16,8185]` inner code? Concatenation with the full-length Reed–Solomon code `[65536,73,65464]_{2^16}` would give a binary `[2^30,1168,≥535822840]` code. This gateway lies outside the 32,768-block rank-16 obstruction proved here.
posts.subject: Concrete k=1168 inner-code gateway
